metadata.Long Title: An Act to prohibit the giving or taking of dowry.
metadata.Department: Department of WOMAN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT
metadata.Type: CENTRAL ACT (Ministry of Women and Child Development, )
metadata.Notification: 1st July, 1961, vide notification No. S.O. 1410, dated 20th June, 1961, see Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part II, sec. 3(ii).

sections.content_text: (1) This Act may be called the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961. (2) It extends to the whole of India. (3) It shall come into force on such date as the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint.
sections.footnote_text: The words 'except the State of Jammu and Kashmir' omitted by Act 34 of 2019. 1st July, 1961, vide notification No. S.O. 1410.

sections.content_text: In this Act, 'dowry' means any property or valuable security given or agreed to be given either directly or indirectly-- (a) by one party to a marriage to the other party to the marriage; or (b) by the parents of either party to a marriage or by any other person, to either party to the marriage or to any other person; at or before or any time after the marriage in connection with the marriage of the said parties, but does not include dower or mahr in the case of persons to whom the Muslim Personal Law (Shariat) applies.

sections.section_title: Penalty for giving or taking dowry.
sections.content_text: If any person, after the commencement of this Act, gives or takes or abets the giving or taking of dowry, he shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than five years, and with fine which shall not be less than fifteen thousand rupees or the amount of the value of such dowry, whichever is more: Provided that the Court may, for adequate and special reasons to be recorded in the judgment, impose a sentence of imprisonment for a term of less than five years. (2) Nothing in sub-section (1) shall apply to presents which are given at the time of a marriage to the bride or bridegroom without any demand having been made in that behalf, provided such presents are entered in a list maintained in accordance with the rules.

If any person demands, directly or indirectly, from the parents or other relatives or guardian of a bride or bridegroom, as the case may be, any dowry, he shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than six months, but which may extend to two years and with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees.

If any person offers, through any advertisement, any share in his property as consideration for marriage, or prints or publishes such advertisement, he shall be punishable with imprisonment up to five years or fine up to fifteen thousand rupees.

sections.section_title: Agreement for giving or taking dowry to be void.
sections.content_text: Any agreement for the giving or taking of dowry shall be void.

sections.section_title: Dowry to be for the benefit of the wife or her heirs.
sections.content_text: Where any dowry is received by any person other than the woman in connection with whose marriage it is given, that person shall transfer it to the woman within three months. If the person fails to transfer, he shall be punishable with imprisonment and fine. Where the woman dies within seven years of marriage otherwise than due to natural causes, the property shall be transferred to her parents or children.

No Court inferior to that of a Metropolitan Magistrate or a Judicial Magistrate of the first class shall try any offence under this Act. No court shall take cognizance except upon its own knowledge or a police report or a complaint by the person aggrieved or a recognised welfare institution.

sections.section_title: Offences to be cognizable and non-bailable.
sections.content_text: The Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 shall apply to offences under this Act as if they were cognizable offences for investigation purposes. Every offence under this Act shall be non-bailable and non-compoundable.

sections.section_title: Burden of proof in certain cases.
sections.content_text: Where any person is prosecuted for taking or abetting the taking of any dowry under section 3, or the demanding of dowry under section 4, the burden of proving that he had not committed an offence under those sections shall be on him.

The State Government may appoint Dowry Prohibition Officers who shall see that the provisions of this Act are complied with, prevent the taking or demanding of dowry, collect evidence for prosecution, and perform additional functions as assigned.
The Central Government may make rules for carrying out the purposes of this Act, including the form and manner of maintaining lists of presents.

sections.section_title: Power of the State Government to make rules.
sections.content_text: The State Government may make rules for additional functions of Dowry Prohibition Officers and the limitations and conditions subject to which they exercise their functions.
